items.title: An 8.8% Income On LMT Stock, For Giving Up Gains Above 9.4%
items.summary: For Lockheed Martin shareholders, here is a trade that pays you a real income today, which you keep no matter what, in exchange for agreeing to sell your stock at a higher price if it gets there.

items.title: Joby builds defense muscle with $500M buy of Resonant Sciences
items.summary: Joby Aviation is buying defense contractor Resonant Sciences in a $500 million deal.

items.title: GE Stock Keeps Climbing. Should You Climb On?
items.summary: This jet engine powerhouse is flying high on real business strength, forcing investors to ask a disciplined question: is the engine's power already reflected in the ticket price.

items.title: 2 Industrials Stocks to Research Further and 1 We Avoid
items.summary: Industrials businesses quietly power the physical things we depend on, from cars and homes to e-commerce infrastructure. But they are at the whim of volatile macroeconomic factors that influence capital spending (like interest rates), and the industry has underperformed the market over the past six months as its 1.3% return lagged the S&P 500 by 9.7 percentage points.

items.title: Rocket Lab Stock's Surge Was Booked Before It Was Priced
items.summary: The defense launch demand behind Rocket Lab stock's run was visible in the company's own contract announcements months before the market paid for it.

items.title: Embraer's Second-Quarter Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates
items.summary: EMBJ beats Q2 earnings and revenue estimates as deliveries and backlog climb, while stronger margins and cash flow drive a higher 2026 outlook.

items.title: U.S. Senate passes stopgap spending bill without Trump priorities
items.summary: Investing.com -- The U.S. Senate approved a short-term spending bill intended to prevent a government shutdown before November’s midterm elections, leaving out President Donald Trump’s requests for Iran war funding and new voter identification measures, Bloomberg reported.

items.title: U.S. plans $1 billion security aid package for Colombia
items.summary: Investing.com -- The Trump administration plans to provide $1 billion in security assistance to the government of Colombia’s newly inaugurated President Abelardo De La Espriella, Reuters reported on Friday, citing the U.S. State Department.
